items.content: `start_backend` is an `async` Tauri command but it acquires `state.backend.lock()` — a synchronous `std::sync::Mutex` guard — and then holds it across a `?`-propagating call into `SidecarManager::start_python_backend(&app)`, which spawns a process and creates a tokio task. A `std::sync::MutexGuard` is not `Send`, and even ignoring the compiler constraints, holding a blocking lock across await/process-spawn points is a hang risk: any other command touching `backend` (e.g. `stop_backend`) blocks the worker thread for the whole spawn duration. Additionally, `start_backend` is invoked *from inside* `.setup()` (see below), so a failure path can deadlock the runtime. Keep the lock scope minimal — release it before the potentially slow spawn, or switch `AppState` to an async-aware primitive (`tokio::sync::Mutex`) / a `try_lock` fast path.

Additionally the script never checks whether `git` itself exists, so a `FileNotFoundError` will escape as an unhandled traceback. Validate `returncode` (and handle `FileNotFoundError`) before using the output.

A ConnectionRefusedError therefore triggers `self.start()` even when `auto_reconnect` is False, contradicting the flag. Unguarded payload parsing: `json.loads(content)` is executed for every message before `msg_type` is inspected. For message types whose content is not JSON (e.g. type 50001 read receipts) this raises `json.JSONDecodeError`, which propagates out of the callback and tears down the socket. Wrap the parsing in try/except so one malformed frame does not kill the connection.

`on_close` unconditionally calls `self.start_ws()` to reconnect before the close message is printed. When the live room has ended (or the server closes the socket permanently), `run_forever` returns immediately after each reconnect attempt, producing an unbounded, tight reconnect loop that repeatedly hammers the Douyin API and spawns a new `ping` thread on every `on_open`. The comment even states the intent to check whether reconnection is needed, but no such check exists. Add a retry limit/backoff and only reconnect when the room is actually still live.

`on_close` calls `self.start_ws()` before the close diagnostics are printed and, more importantly, unconditionally. When the room has ended the server closes the socket, `run_forever` returns immediately, and each `on_close` schedules another `start_ws`, producing an unbounded tight reconnect loop that repeatedly hammers the Douyin API. The inline comment states the intent to check whether reconnection is needed, but no such check exists — add a retry cap/backoff and verify the room is still live.

items.content: `escape_digest` scans forward through `digest` starting at `idx` and, once `idx >= len(digest)`, repeatedly returns `fallback`. If `fallback == reserved`, the `while v == reserved` loop never terminates (infinite loop), and even when it does terminate the loop has advanced `idx` past the end so the fallback is index-independent — verify the reserved/fallback invariants hold for all call sites (3/11/12, 4/8/9, 5/12/13). At minimum the fallback should be guaranteed `!= reserved`.

`trans_cookies()` calls `cookies_str.split("; ")`, which raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'split'` when the env var is missing. `perepare_auth` also does `self.cookie.pop(...)` on the result, so a `None` cookie string is never tolerated. Similarly, `os.path.join(..., f'{excel_name}.xlsx')` in main.py fails for the same reason. Add an explicit guard/validation so a missing `DY_COOKIES`/`DY_LIVE_COOKIES` produces a clear, actionable error instead of a confusing AttributeError deep inside cookie parsing.

`download_media` shadows the built-in `type` and, more importantly, this function has no timeout on `requests.get`. If the remote server stalls, the call blocks indefinitely; combined with `@retry(tries=3)` on the caller, a single hung download can hang the whole application. Always pass a `timeout` (and consider `raise_for_status()` to detect HTTP errors, which are currently written as garbage content to disk).

`norm_text` (and thus the whole xlsx export) crashes when any value is `None`, because `str(v)` is evaluated before `norm_text` and the regex `sub` on `'None'` is fine — but `None` fields such as `title`/`desc` are instead stringified to the literal "None". More critically, `handle_work_info` reads nested keys like `data['author']['avatar_thumb']['url_list'][0]`, `data['video']['cover']['url_list'][0]` and `data['statistics']['comment_count']` without any guarding; if the list is empty (`url_list == []`) or a key is missing, this raises `IndexError`/`KeyError` for the whole batch. items.content: `asyncio.create_task(adm.start(cfg))` is fire-and-forget: the task object is never stored or awaited, so if `adm.start` raises (e.g. the `RuntimeError("当前状态 ... 无法启动")` guard in `AutoDM.start`), the exception is never retrieved and is silently swallowed — the surrounding `try/except` cannot catch it, and the route still returns `{"ok": True}`. Keep a reference (e.g. `request.app.state.start_task = asyncio.create_task(...)`) and attach a done-callback that logs `task.exception()` so startup failures surface instead of being lost.

Check-then-act race on `adm.state`: this guard only reads the state, but the transition to `EngineState.STARTING` happens inside the background `start()` coroutine (line 393 of `core/auto_dm.py`), which does not run until the event loop yields. Two concurrent `/start` requests can both observe `IDLE`/`STOPPED`, both pass the check, and both schedule `adm.start`, causing the loser to raise `RuntimeError` (silently swallowed by the un-awaited task). Reserve the state atomically here (set `adm.state = EngineState.STARTING`) or have `AutoDM.start` perform the transition synchronously before any `await`, so the guard is authoritative.

items.content: `_read_tail` reads and parses the **entire** file before slicing `out[-limit:]`, whereas the no-`name` branch accumulates directly into `list[tuple]` and slices. Worse, `run_*.log` is written with `rotation="20 MB"`, so a single session file can exceed 20 MB; a `name=<file>` request therefore parses tens of thousands of lines, and the guard `name.endswith(".log")` in the helper ties this helper to the run-file naming while the merged branch reads any `*.log`. items.content: `_port_open` performs a synchronous blocking TCP `connect_ex` (confirmed in `auto_dm/accounts.py`, timeout=0.3s). Calling it twice directly inside this `async def` handler blocks the event loop for up to ~0.6s on every `/overview` poll, stalling all other requests/tasks. Run the probes off the event loop, e.g. `b_alive, r_alive = await asyncio.gather(asyncio.to_thread(_daemon_alive, bport), asyncio.to_thread(_daemon_alive, rport))`.

`r.json()` is called unconditionally. The module itself documents (see `/liked`, `/user/works`) that Douyin frequently returns HTTP 200 with a 0-byte body; on that path `r.json()` raises `JSONDecodeError`, which propagates out of the whole batch loop and aborts all remaining chunks instead of being skipped like a non-zero `status_code`. Guard with a body-length/try-except check and `continue` on the failed chunk.

`body.resolved()` returns a normalized `TaskConfig` in which `dm_pool` is already collapsed to `list[str]` (see models/task.py `resolved()`: `dm_pool=[t if isinstance(t, str) else t.get("text", "") for t in dm_pool]`). Persisting that value into `kv_store["config"]["dm_pool"]` destroys the per-item `enabled` flags, so after a reload the pool's enable/disable state is silently lost. Note `save_dm_pool()` (POST /dm-pool) correctly stores `[{"text", "enabled"}]` — the two write paths are inconsistent. Persist the same structure here (e.g. `adm.dm_template`, which holds the `[{"text", "enabled"}]` form) instead of `cfg.dm_pool`.

`_dm_pool_from_adm` builds items from `adm.dm_template` as `{"text": item.get("text", ""), "enabled": ...}`, but `DispatchCenter` records use `content`/`comment`/`send_ts`/`send_at`/`captured_at` (see models/task.py `SendRecord`). The export iterates `adm.dispatch.records` and reads `r.get("capture_ts")`/`r.get("send_ts")`, which do not exist on `SendRecord` — the time columns (捕获时间/发送时间) come out empty. Also the dict branch reads the wrong field name for the record key. Use `captured_at`/`sent_at` (or reuse `_records_from_adm`, which already maps `sent_at` -> `send_ts`) instead of `capture_ts`/`send_ts`.

`load_dotenv(env_path, override=True)` is a process-wide side effect (it writes into `os.environ`) that runs on every `enrich_auth` call. In this backend (single process, many accounts — see the note in `DYLoginApi._load_auth_from_env`, which deliberately switched to `dotenv_values` for exactly this reason) the last imported account's `DY_COOKIES`/credentials will silently overwrite the previously loaded ones, so any code that later reads `os.getenv("DY_COOKIES")` can get another account's cookies. Since the subsequent `_load_auth_from_env(env_path)` already reads the file directly (and falls back to `os.getenv` only when the file is missing), this call is not needed here — either drop it or use `dotenv_values` for a pure file read.

items.content: `_pid_running` is called outside the lock but is the guard that keeps a *recycled* PID from being killed. Since callers (e.g. `daemon_launcher._spawn_sidecar`) can `register()` new PIDs from other threads at any time, the current structure has two defects: (1) `alive_pids()`/`kill_all()` can race with registration, and more importantly (2) a PID is read and cleared from the ledger, then checked with `_pid_running` — during that window the OS may have recycled the PID for an unrelated process, so `taskkill /F /T` would kill a process this process never spawned. That directly violates the module's stated '铁律'. Consider validating the PID identity (e.g. record the process start time via psutil and re-check it before killing) and/or holding the ledger entry until the kill attempt completes.

`db.transaction('user', 'readonly')` can throw synchronously (e.g. the connection was closed/invalidated by a version upgrade or a stray `db.close()`), and this call is NOT wrapped in try/catch unlike the surrounding `open(dn)` call. Such a throw propagates out of the `await new Promise(...)` executor — an async executor's throw rejects the promise — aborting the whole `for (const dn of userDbs)` loop and discarding `out.users` already collected from prior DBs, ultimately rejecting the JS expression and surfacing as an empty/error result. Wrap the transaction body (and `db.close()`) in try/catch and `continue` on failure so one bad DB cannot wipe the entire read.

items.content: `wait_if_paused` places the `should_cancel` check *before* the pause check, so the documented contract — “paused 时阻塞等待” — is violated: if a task is paused and then canceled, the very first loop iteration returns `False` without ever honoring a pending pause. In the call path `downloader.py` only checks `should_cancel`, so any caller relying on `wait_if_paused` to honor pause semantics will mis-handle paused-then-canceled tasks. More importantly, the loop is unbounded: it spins forever (0.2s poll) if the task_id is never resumed — nothing ever removes the flag for a task that is dropped from `_tasks` (e.g. via `cleanup_finished`), so a paused task that is cleaned up leaks a thread spinning forever. Consider re-checking the task’s existence/terminal state inside the loop and exiting (returning `False`) when the task is gone, and move the cancel check after the pause check (or document/refine the ordering).

`headers.with_bd(api, auth)` returns `self` in `builder/header.py`? No — `Header.with_bd` returns `self`, but `Header.with_csrf` does NOT return anything (see `builder/header.py:30-31`), yet here it is chained onto the result of `with_bd(...)`. As written, `with_csrf` is called on the return value of `with_bd`, and since `with_csrf` returns `None`, the subsequent `headers.set_header(...)` calls do not raise, but `headers` is the object built by `with_bd` only if it returns self. In the current builder, `with_bd` returns `self` (line 24). However, note the true latent bug: the csrf token is silently dropped whenever the underlying `with_csrf` returns None and its return value is what subsequent header calls operate on. Please make `with_csrf` return `self` (consistent with other `with_*` methods) and avoid relying on the builder's return values, e.g. assign `headers.with_csrf(auth.cookie_str)` without depending on a return.

items.content: `verify=False` disables TLS certificate verification on both the GET and POST exits, so responses can be silently intercepted/tampered with (MITM). Given the client carries the user's session cookies, this is a real security risk rather than a style issue. At minimum make it configurable (e.g. `verify=cls.verify_tls` defaulting to True) and only disable it for a documented reason; the same applies to the `requests.post(...)` call below.

Operator precedence bug: `A or B and C` parses as `A or (B and C)`. So `ConnectionRefusedError` triggers a reconnect unconditionally, ignoring `self.auto_reconnect`. Also `type(error) == X` should use `isinstance` to also catch subclasses. Add explicit parentheses and use `isinstance`.

`on_message` unpacks nested attributes and indexes deeply nested dict keys (`content["url"]["url_list"][0]`, `content["resource_url"][...][0]`) with no validation. The payload comes from a remote WebSocket peer, so a missing/empty key or malformed JSON raises an unhandled exception (IndexError/KeyError/JSONDecodeError) inside the websocket callback, killing the receive loop. Guard the parsing and validate required fields/lists before indexing.

`WebSocketApp` accepts `cookie=` only via the `header` dict in most `websocket-client` versions; there is no `cookie` keyword parameter. Passing `cookie=self.auth.cookie_str` may raise `TypeError` at runtime (or be silently ignored). Prefer adding `'Cookie': self.auth.cookie_str` into the `header` dict.

SigV4 canonical query mismatch: the request URL is built from the insertion order of `q` (`Action, Version, SpaceName`) and without `_uri_encode`, while the signature is computed over `canonical_query`, which is sorted (`Action, SpaceName, Version`) and URI-encoded. AWS SigV4 requires the canonical query string to match the actual request URL exactly; using a different order/encoding will produce an `AuthorizationHeaderMalformed`/signature error (or intermittent success only when the dict order happens to align). Reuse `canonical_query` for the URL, as `apply_upload` already does.

items.content: `ping` is a plain `while True` with no termination condition of its own. When `ws.close()` is called the next `send` typically fails and breaks the loop, but if the socket stays half-open (no exception on send, e.g. buffered write to a dead peer) the loop spins forever, sleeping 5s each turn — leaking one thread per (re)connection, since `start_ws` is called repeatedly from `on_close`. Suggest making the loop honour a per-connection stop flag (checked on `_should_stop`/a dedicated `threading.Event` set in `on_close`) plus a send-failure counter.

`on_close` calls `self.start_ws()` synchronously and unconditionally (except after a deliberate stop). `run_forever` runs on the caller's thread, so a persistently failing endpoint (expired cookie, room closed, DNS/network error) becomes an unbounded tight reconnect loop with no delay and no backoff, hammering Douyin and burning CPU/network. Add a small sleep between attempts, a bounded retry/backoff, and only retry when the room is still live (the comment says this check is pending but it is not implemented).

items.content: `destroy_session` unconditionally deletes the shared persisted session file, ignoring whether the passed `token` actually matches the session stored in it. If a stale/foreign token is presented (e.g. an old tab logs out after a newer login), this wipes the *valid* on-disk session of the currently logged-in member, and `restore_persisted_session()` will then fail after restart. Guard the deletion: only remove the file when the on-disk token equals the token being destroyed (or when the caller is the active session).

`accounts_root()` resolves the member id twice with *different* fallback rules. `member_space_root()` can succeed via `_session_file_member_id()` while the re-resolution below (`current_member_id() or DY_MEMBER or _session_file_member_id()`) may still be consistent — but when all three are empty while `member_space_root()` returned a path (or if any of these mutate between the two calls), the final `or ""` passes an **empty string** to `member_store.member_accounts_dir("")`, which does `os.makedirs(members_root()/auto_dm/accounts)` — the exact empty-id path the docstring says it is trying to avoid. Resolve the id once and reuse it (or return None when it is empty) instead of calling the helper twice.

On registry read failure the loader logs the error but returns an empty registry, and the caller may then save it back. For write paths this means a transient/parse error (or a partially written file) silently discards every existing member record on the next `register_member`/`change_password`. Since the log says "避免误删" (avoid accidental deletion) this contradicts the behavior — a read failure on a write path should abort the write instead of persisting an empty table.

items.content: `_migrate_v1` sets the `model_hub.migrated` guard flag BEFORE it knows whether the migration will actually succeed. If anything inside the subsequent `try` fails (e.g. `ai_reply.get_config()` raises), the flag stays `True` while no data was migrated, and the outer `except` just returns the raw data. Later `_load()` calls will see `migrated_v1` absent and non-empty-free data, skip migration forever, and the old v1 config is silently lost. Set the flag only after `_save(out)` succeeds (or clear it on failure).

`_embed` internally truncates to 20 texts (`_ai._embed_failover(texts[:20], ...)`), but `_dedup_check` passes `[content] + [it["content"] for it in candidates]` unbounded. When a topic has >19 existing entries the returned vector count no longer matches, `len(vecs) != len(candidates) + 1` becomes true, and the function silently returns `(None, 0.0)` — disabling dedup entirely with no signal. This is exactly the >20 failure mode already worked around in `semantic_topk` via batching. `_scan_duplicates` (line ~640) has the same unbounded `_embed` call and silently skips any topic group larger than 20. Batch these calls (chunks of ≤20) or raise `_embed`'s truncation limit.

Threshold is compared against the decayed score (`best_score`), but the docstring explicitly says the threshold applies to the raw relevance, not the decayed score. Since `_decay()` is always ≤ 1, the effective threshold is effectively raised (e.g. an item 50 days old must reach raw ≥ 1.43 to pass 0.85), so older-but-relevant entries are silently never matched. Also, `best_raw` and `best_score` are only assigned inside the loop, so if no candidate has `raw > 0` they are never initialized — a NameError waiting to happen if the code later references them. Compute the candidate's raw score, gate on `raw >= threshold`, and rank by the decayed score (or explicitly separate the two).

`shutdown()` only sets `_sched_stop`, but the module never creates a scheduler thread and never reads `_sched_stop`/`_sched_thread` anywhere. The module docstring promises "后台单线程 `_probe_scheduler` 按账号错峰刷新（避免同秒并发打网），把各调用方的零散需求收敛为「每账号每 DY_UID_PROBE_TTL 秒至多 1 次」", but no such thread is ever started. As a result the only refresh paths are the caller-driven `get_uid` and the startup one-shot `warm_all`, so the advertised "每账号每 DY_UID_PROBE_TTL 秒至多 1 次" convergence is not actually enforced for the whole process lifetime — the core anti-风控 guarantee this refactor was written for is missing. Either implement the scheduler (a daemon thread that periodically calls `_do_probe`/`refresh_now` with per-account staggering, checking `_sched_stop`), or remove the claim from the docstring and stop advertising `shutdown()`.

When the probe result is rejected as inconsistent, the function returns `None` **without writing anything to `_cache`**. Since the rejection path is exactly the case where `DouyinAPI.get_my_uid` keeps returning the same stale value, every subsequent `get_uid(name)` call will miss the cache, acquire the lock and probe the network again — the 300s/60s anti-风控 TTL is completely bypassed for such accounts, which is the worst possible case (repeated query/user on every call). Write a negative/backoff cache entry (e.g. `_cache[name] = (time.time(), None)`) before returning so the failure backoff applies.

items.content: The module docstring promises "若已被导入则强制重定位其 DB 路径", but no such logic exists. If `database` (or `config.settings`) was already imported by an earlier test module before this one at a different `DY_APP_ROOT`, nothing here re-points it: `database._conn` is left open on the old DB file and `config.settings.data_dir` is baked in from the old root, so config tests keep sharing polluted state — the exact failure mode this module claims to fix. Note `fresh()` also only evicts `database` from `sys.modules`; it never calls `database.reset_connection()` before the delete, so an already-open connection/`_conn` is leaked and the old DB file handle stays around. Implement the promised relocation (e.g. call `database.reset_connection()` and re-import, and reset `config.settings`), or drop the claim from the docstring.

`_wipe()` 直接用 `get_db()` 拿到全局连接并执行 DELETE，属于对生产库路径的直连写入；而 `_ROOT` 只在 `DY_APP_ROOT` 生效时才被使用，若 `member_ctx.db_path()` 已登录并返回了别的路径，本用例会清掉真实会员数据库中的 `model_hub` 配置（`test_migrate_from_v1` 更是先删掉 `migrated` 标记再写入伪造的 v1 结构）。测试应显式将数据库指向临时目录（如设置 `DB_PATH`/mock `database._db_path`）后再执行写入，避免误伤真实数据。

items.content: `setUp` does not neutralize the environment variables `DY_SEND_MIN_INTERVAL` / `DY_SEND_MAX_WAIT`. `app_config.get` falls back to `_from_env` when no stored value exists, so on a machine where these env vars are set (they are read by both `recv_daemon._FALLBACK_*` and the schema `env` mapping) the "default" assertions will see the env value instead of the schema default, making the test results environment-dependent. `test_fallback_when_app_config_broken` also patches `ac.get` to always raise, so it silently passes through the env path too — it verifies the module-level env override rather than the intended code-level constant. Explicitly clear/set these env vars in `setUp`/`tearDown` (e.g. via `unittest.mock.patch.dict(os.environ, ...)`).

The public key parsing silently assumes `pub_hex` starts with a 2-char uncompressed-point prefix (e.g. "04") and unconditionally strips `pub_hex[2:]`. If a caller passes the raw `X||Y` hex without a prefix (as `get_ree_key`'s base64 form lacks), the first byte of X is dropped and verification silently fails or returns wrong results. Moreover, `bytes.fromhex(pub_hex[2:])` and the `VerifyingKey.from_string(...)` call are OUTSIDE the `try`, so malformed/odd-length input raises an exception instead of the documented `False` return. Move the key construction inside the `try` and validate the prefix explicitly.

The wrapper is not transparent to loguru's `**kwargs`. loguru treats extra keyword arguments as *named format values* (options like traceback control must be passed via `logger.opt(exception=True)`, not as kwargs), so re-emitting the call as `orig_(msg, **kwargs)` leaves those kwargs dangling against a merged message that no longer contains any `{placeholder}` for them. A real call site does exactly this: `browser_daemon.py:771` calls `logger.error("BCC-006", "...", exc_info=True)` — after this patch the args are folded into the text but `exc_info=True` is still forwarded to loguru, which does not understand `exc_info` (loguru uses `exception=`/`logger.opt`), so the intended traceback is silently lost. Consider stripping/translating known non-format kwargs, or better, only merge when there are no kwargs, so loguru's option semantics are preserved.

`load_env` rebinds the module-level globals `dy_auth`/`dy_live_auth` on every call. It is invoked concurrently for different accounts (e.g. `api/linkmic.py` and `api/platform.py` request paths). A `load_env(env_path_for_account_B)` can therefore overwrite the global `dy_auth` that an in-flight request for account A is still using, silently cross-wiring credentials. Prefer returning per-call auth objects to callers and avoid mutating shared module state, or guard access with a lock.

On any failure the except block returns the tuple `(None, None)`. All callers immediately subscript the result, e.g. `builder/header.py`: `generate_csrf_token(cookie_str)[0]`. When the request fails, `csrf_token_1` is `None`, so `[0]` raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable`, crashing the request path instead of degrading gracefully. Return an empty string (or a namedtuple/dict) so callers get a safe default, e.g. `return '', ''`.
items.existing_code:
except Exception as e:
        return csrf_token_1, csrf_token_2
items.suggestion_code:
except Exception:
        return '', ''

A future reader editing this version will see no effect. Delete the shadowed definition (or merge into a single, documented function).

items.content: `_pw`, `_browser`, `context`, `_backend` are assigned inside the `try`, but the `finally` reads `_backend`. The `except RuntimeError` around the launch only catches `RuntimeError`; if `launch_async`/`should_use_vb` raises any other exception (e.g. `TimeoutError`, `OSError`, `playwright` errors, `asyncio.CancelledError`), it propagates before the `finally` — that is fine since `try` starts after the call. However if `page = context.pages[0] if ...` or `context.new_page()` raises after a successful launch, the exception escapes with no cleanup at all, because the `try/finally` only covers the scan loop. Wrap the whole post-launch section (including `goto`/`new_page`) in the `try` so the browser is always torn down, and initialize `_backend = None` before the launch call for defensive clarity.

The stylesheet references CSS custom properties (`--foreground`, `--muted-foreground`, `--border`, `--card`) that are never defined anywhere in this file, and no external stylesheet is linked. When this standalone HTML is opened directly, these variables are invalid, so `color`/`border`/`background` declarations fall back to their initial values (transparent border, default black text) — the entire mock renders incorrectly. Either declare the variables in `:root` or link the theme stylesheet.

items.content: `lucide-react` has no released 1.x line on the public npm registry (its versions are `0.4xx`). A `^1.45.0` range only resolves via a third-party mirror (see package-lock.json `registry.npmmirror.com`), so a clean `npm install` against the default registry will fail and any install pulls a non-canonical artifact — a reproducibility / supply-chain risk. Pin to the real published version (e.g. `^0.4xx`) or document the mirror requirement.

Header merge order is inverted: `headers` is spread after `...init`, so any caller-supplied `init.headers` completely overrides the default headers — including `Content-Type`, `X-App-Version` and the `X-Member-Token` auth token. This silently drops authentication for such requests, producing 401s. Put `...init` first so the auth/content headers always win (or explicitly merge them).

Missing 401 handling that exists in `client.ts`. All `/api/*` routes require `X-Member-Token` (main.py:583-623) and return 401 when the session expires. `client.ts` clears the stored token on 401 so the UI observes logged-out state and returns to the login page; this wrapper does not, so an expired session causes every platform call to throw a plain `Error` while the stale token stays in `localStorage`, leaving the user stuck on repeated failures instead of being redirected to login.

The review table is always empty: `rows` is a local constant initialized to `[]` and never populated (no props/state/derivation feed it). Consequences: `filtered`, `cnt()` and all `rows.filter(...)` calls always return nothing, so the table always renders the "暂无评论记录" empty state, and comment history is never reachable. Either derive `rows` from real data (e.g. from `account`/query cache) with `useMemo`, or remove the unused table until data is wired up.

`batchExport` is a no-op that reports success: it never exports anything, yet pushes "已导出 N 个账号的运行数据". This misleads the user into believing data was exported (and could be relied on for backup). Either implement the actual export/download or remove the button and handler.

Hardcoded backend base URL (`http://127.0.0.1:8000`) bypasses the shared `api` client. Besides the checklist rule against hardcoded URL paths, this breaks in packaged builds / non-default ports and duplicates auth plumbing. Add an `ensureBcc`/`ensureRecv` method to the API client (or reuse an existing helper) and call it through `api`. The same issue appears in the `ensure-recv` fetch below.

`a.name` is used without a null check for `.length` (line 159) and string concatenation (line 194). `name` is declared as a required `string` in `RawAccount`, but the data comes from the backend and may be missing/undefined; `a.name.length` would then throw a TypeError during render (the very failure mode this mapper is meant to guard against). Consider `const name = a.name || "—"` at the top of `mapAcct` and reuse it.

items.content: `sendBatch` performs an outward-facing bulk private-message operation (up to 200 candidates, `max_send: 0`, `interval: 0`) with no confirmation dialog and no rate limiting despite the UI showing a `rate_limited` counter. An accidental click immediately blasts messages to all matched comment users. Given this is an irreversible user-facing action, add a confirmation step before dispatching the batch (and consider a sane default interval/max_send).

`applyMut.onSuccess` only handles the `d.ok` success path. When the server returns `{ ok: false }` (or an error payload), nothing is reported to the user and the failure is silently swallowed, leaving the UI in an inconsistent state. Add an `else` branch that surfaces the error, consistent with `scanMut`/`patchMut`.

`restoreMut.onSuccess` unconditionally pushes "已恢复" without checking `d.ok`. If the restore request fails at the application level (`ok: false`), the user is told the item was restored when it was not, and the recycle list is refreshed to the server's (unchanged) data. Guard on `d.ok` and surface the failure otherwise.

The disabled condition is inverted relative to intent: `!q && !a` only disables the button when BOTH fields are empty. Filling just one field (e.g. question only) leaves the button enabled, so an item can be saved with an empty question or empty answer, producing an unusable/never-matchable KB entry. Use `!q || !a` (ideally also `.trim()`).

items.content: Effect dependency `onLogin` is unstable. In App.tsx the prop is passed as an inline arrow `onLogin={(u) => { setMemberName(u); ... }}`, so its identity changes on every parent render (App re-renders frequently due to its 3s polling). Since `onLogin` is in the dependency array, this effect re-runs repeatedly while `checking === true` (no token, or token present but not logged in), firing duplicate `/api/member/state` requests and allowing race conditions / duplicate flushes. Keep the startup check as a one-shot (empty deps) and, if needed, hold the callback in a ref.

Async IIFE in useEffect has no try/catch. Although `memberApi.state()` catches internally today, `onLogin(s.username)` is a caller-supplied callback that can throw, and any future change to `state()` (e.g. rethrow on network error) would leave an unhandled promise rejection and, worse, leave `checking` stuck at `true` forever, permanently trapping the user on the "正在检查登录态…" splash. Wrap the body in try/catch and always `setChecking(false)` on failure to guarantee the gate resolves.

`recordsToRows` 接收的记录来自后端 `_records_from_adm`（`getCurrentTask` 与历史任务快照同源），每条记录字段为 `captured_at` / `send_ts` / `send_at`，**并不存在 `start_ts`**。因此该表达式恒为 `""`，查阅模式表格的「时间」列会始终为空。应与 live-page.tsx 的实时行保持一致，用 `fmtTime(r.captured_at)`（`captured_at` 为秒级时间戳）。

Provide a default/optional-chain fallback, e.g. `const push = props.push ?? (() => {})` or guard the call with `props.push?.(...)`.

A text containing shortcodes like `[constructor]`, `[toString]`, `[valueOf]`, `[hasOwnProperty]` will match this expression and return a function instead of `undefined`, causing the falsy guard to pass and then React to attempt rendering a function as a child (throwing an error / breaking the message list). Use an own-property check or `Object.create(null)`/`Map`.

items.content: Bug: the effect only runs once on mount with `[]` deps, but at that moment `media` is typically `null`, so the component returns `null` early and `rootRef.current` is still `null`. The `if (el)` guard then silently skips attaching the listener, and because deps are empty the effect never re-runs when the modal actually opens — so the native wheel handler (and the intended page-scroll prevention) never takes effect. Depend on `media` (or use a callback ref) so the listener is attached when the root node actually exists.

`qc.invalidateQueries()` with no arguments invalidates every query in the cache (including `accounts`, overview polling, live-monitor queries, etc.), forcing a full application-wide refetch storm after each 更新会话. Scope it to the affected keys: `qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["msg-convs"] })` (and `["msg-detail"]` if needed).

`toggleRun` inspects `enabled` (server config flag) to decide start vs stop, but the button label/color are driven by `running`. When they diverge — e.g. `enabled === true` but `running === false` (the UI renders "启动监听") — clicking the button calls `api.aiStop()`, i.e. a button labelled "启动" performs a stop. Decide based on the same value that drives the UI (e.g. `running ? aiStop() : aiStart()`) so the action matches the label; also `toggleRun`'s `useCallback` deps should then track that value.

`registerKernel(name, factory)` accepts arbitrary keys without validating `name` (empty string, `__proto__`, `constructor`, `toString`...). Assigning to `REGISTRY["__proto__"]` pollutes `Object.prototype` instead of storing an own property, and `pickKernel` does truthiness checks (`REGISTRY.hls`) that can be satisfied by inherited properties of `Object.prototype` (e.g. after such pollution `REGISTRY.html5` would be overshadowed only for matching key, but any inherited truthy value for `hls`/`dash` would be invoked as a factory). Use a prototype-less map (`Object.create(null)` / `new Map()`) and reject unsafe/empty names.

The load-timeout retry calls `v.load()` but never re-arms the timeout and never calls `set("load")` again. It also leaves the timer id in `timerRef` pointing at a fired timer. Consequence: only ONE retry is ever possible (the second/third attempts never get a chance to mark `readyState < 3`), so `PLAYER_VIDEO_MAX_AUTO_RETRIES` is effectively dead and a stalled video never reaches the `error` state — it hangs on the "加载中…"/"缓冲中…" hint forever. Encapsulate the check in a function that re-arms itself after each `v.load()` and returns a promise so it can be `await`ed.

The resume-position logic runs immediately after `await k.attach(...)`, i.e. before the media metadata is loaded. `v.duration` is `NaN` at that point, so the `Number.isFinite(v.duration)` guard is always false and `v.currentTime = pos` is never executed — the documented "续播" (resume playback) feature never works. Apply the position inside the `loadedmetadata` handler instead (or await metadata before seeking), and guard with the `canplay`/`loadeddata` event.

`videoRef.current` will be `null` on this effect's first run when `media.type === "video"`, because the `<video>` element is only rendered after the early returns for `!media` / `failed`. In that case the effect bails out without ever setting status to "load" or attaching a kernel, so switching from a non-video media to a video leaves the stage in `idle` and the video is never wired up. Render the `<video>` element unconditionally (hidden when not needed) or track the element in state so the effect re-runs once it is mounted.

Drag state can get stuck at `true`. Only `onPointerUp` resets `dragging.current`; there is no `onPointerCancel` handler and no `releasePointerCapture`. If the pointer interaction is cancelled (touch interrupted, pointer leaves/loses capture, or component unmounts mid-drag), `dragging.current` stays `true` forever and the rAF tick permanently stops updating `cur`/`dur`, freezing the progress bar. Also, `setPointerCapture` is called on `e.target` (a child element) rather than the track element, so cleanup/release is not tied to the same node. Capture on `barRef.current` instead, and reset drag state in an `onPointerCancel` handler.
items.suggestion_code:

Since `setView` blindly casts a `string` to `ViewType` and `VIEW_TITLE` is typed as `Record<ViewType, string>`, a caller doing `setView("home")` compiles fine but persists an untitled view; `App.tsx` then falls back to `VIEW_TITLE[t as ViewType] ?? "控制台"` and renders a nameless tab. Either add the missing members to the union and `VIEW_TITLE`, or derive the type from `SOURCE_VIEWS` (e.g. `type SourceView = (typeof SOURCE_VIEWS)[number]`) so the two definitions cannot drift.

Unvalidated input is persisted and cast to `ViewType`: any string (typo, stale/legacy value in `localStorage`, or a value injected by another script) becomes the current view. A bad persisted value is also re-read on every reload by `readStoredView`, which performs the same unchecked `as ViewType` cast, so the app can get permanently stuck on an unknown view with no title. Validate against a known set (e.g. `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(VIEW_TITLE, v)`) and change the signature to `setView: (v: ViewType) => void` so callers get compile-time safety.

`readStoredView` returns the raw `localStorage` string whenever it is truthy, so any junk value (e.g. a legacy key, a value written by an older bundle, or `"null"`/`"undefined"`) is accepted as a valid `ViewType` without validation. This is the loading half of the same unvalidated-cast problem: it should check the value against the known view keys (`VIEW_TITLE`) before returning it, otherwise `currentView` is typed as `ViewType` while holding a string that is not a valid view.

items.content: `on_open` starts a new `ping` thread on every open, but the old thread is never stopped: the loop in `ping` only exits when `ws.send` raises. Because `on_close` reconnects and creates fresh `WebSocketApp`s, ping threads from previous connections can keep running and holding references, leaking threads (and CPU) over repeated reconnects. Consider tracking and stopping the ping thread, or bounding reconnects.

`on_message` wraps nearly the entire message-handling body in one broad `except Exception` and then just prints `'error'` plus the exception message, silently discarding failures (including a single malformed/unparsable message) so the caller can never tell what failed. Narrow the try block to the parsing that can actually fail, and include enough context (e.g. the item method) when logging the error.

`on_message` calls `gzip.decompress(frame.payload)` unconditionally, but the `compress` query param is only requested as `'gzip'` and for non-gzip frames (or non-payload control frames) this raises, dropping the whole message. Guard on `frame.payloadEncoding == 'gzip'` (or catch the decompression failure separately) before decompressing.

`s.payload = response.internalExt.encode('utf-8')` is sent as the ack payload. Per the referenced protocol the ack payload should echo the frame's internalExt header value (the commented-out line reads it from `frame.headersList[1].value`); using `response.internalExt` may send an incorrect ack value, so the server could fail to stop redelivering messages. Confirm which field the server actually expects before relying on this.

`ping` sends a heartbeat then `time.sleep(5)` inside the loop, but the protobuf field `heartbeatDuration` is hard-coded to `'0'` in the connection params; if the server advertises a heartbeat interval via `LiveResponse.heartbeatDuration`, ignoring it and using a fixed 5s (or 0) is a mismatch that can get the connection closed. Also note the thread only exits when `ws.send` throws, so a send that silently fails on a dead socket leaves the thread spinning forever.

`on_open` spawns a fresh `ping` thread on every open, but nothing stops the previous one: `ping` only exits when `ws.send` raises `Exception`. Because `on_close` reconnects with a new `WebSocketApp`, ping threads from earlier connections can keep running and leak threads (and CPU) across reconnects.

`on_message` calls `gzip.decompress(frame.payload)` unconditionally. While `compress=gzip` is requested, any non-gzip payload (or control frame) will raise here and, because of the broad `except`, silently drop the entire message batch. Check `frame.payloadEncoding` before decompressing, or handle the decompression error separately.

The entire per-message loop is wrapped in one broad `except Exception` that only prints `'error'` and the exception string, silently discarding failures (a single unparsable message aborts processing of all remaining messages in the batch) with no indication of which message failed. items.content: `User.top_fans` references `User` itself, making the message recursive. `User` is populated directly from `PushFrame.payload`/`Message.payload`, i.e. from a remote WebSocket server (see `dy_apis/douyin_recv_msg.py` and `dy_live/server.py` which call `ParseFromString` on untrusted frames). Recursive message definitions have no schema-level depth limit, so a malicious or malformed frame can nest `top_fans` arbitrarily deep and exhaust stack/heap. Consider bounding recursion at the application layer (e.g. reject payloads beyond a max depth/size before parsing) and documenting that boundary.

`LiveResponse.messagesList` is an unbounded `repeated` field that is parsed directly from remote push frames (`response.ParseFromString(origin_bytes)` in `dy_live/server.py`). Because protobuf repeated fields carry no element-count limit, a hostile server can send a frame with a very large number of `Message` entries (or huge `payload`/`internalExt` byte blobs), causing unbounded memory/CPU consumption on parse. Recommend enforcing an application-level maximum frame size and message count before/while parsing, and documenting that limit at this boundary.

Field numbering jumps from 18 to 21, skipping 19 and 20. If those numbers were previously used by removed fields, they should be added to `reserved` to prevent accidental reuse and wire-compatibility breakage; otherwise a comment explaining the gap would help. Also note `ts_sign`, `sdk_cert`, `access`, `biz` and the token-related fields carry authorization/signature material — ensure they are never logged or persisted in plaintext at the service boundary.

`GetConversationInfoListV2RequestBody` embeds `GetConversationInfoListV2ResponseBodyData`, a response-side message, as a request field. Reusing a response message inside a request couples the two contracts: any change to the response shape silently alters the request wire format, and it also duplicates the domain concept. Recommend defining a dedicated request-side message (e.g. `GetConversationInfoListV2RequestParams`) instead.

The `ResponseBody.body` oneof is declared but, per protobuf wire rules, `cmd` (field 1) is the discriminator that tells the client which oneof member is populated. There is no `optional`/sentinel handling and no documentation of the mapping between `cmd` values and the oneof variants. More importantly, if a server sends a `Response` whose `cmd` indicates one variant but the oneof actually holds a different (or no) variant, clients silently fall into an invalid zero-state — the oneof being unset is indistinguishable from "unknown command". Consider modeling an explicit `UNSPECIFIED`/unknown sentinel or documenting the `cmd`→oneof contract so a malformed/unknown response is detectable rather than silently treated as empty.

Note also that `Response` is a very generic top-level message name for a package-less schema; if this .proto is ever merged with others, `Response`, `ResponseBody` and `MessageBody` are likely to collide.

`content` is declared as an unconstrained `string`. In this protocol it carries the serialized protobuf/JSON payload of the actual chat message, which for untrusted peers can be arbitrarily large or deeply nested. A plain `string` gives no length or nesting bound, so a malicious/large message can be accepted and stored/parsed without limit. Consider documenting an application-level size limit (or adding a bounded `bytes` field with validation guidance) at this trust boundary.

items.content: `self.counter` is mutated on every `sign_query` call without any synchronization. If a single signer instance is shared across request threads, `self.counter += 1` is a non-atomic read-modify-write and the counter/`z149_counter_bucket` value can be corrupted, producing non-deterministic signatures. Either document that instances are not thread-safe or use a lock / per-request counter.

`verify_req_sign` is the module's signature-verification API, but it unconditionally strips the first byte of the supplied public key (`pub_hex[2:]`) and assumes SEC1 uncompressed format. If the caller passes a 64-byte raw X||Y key (no leading `04`) — or an odd-length/short hex string — `bytes.fromhex(pub_hex[2:])` silently truncates or raises `ValueError`. Since the slicing/decoding sits outside the `try`, that error escapes instead of returning `False`. Normalize the key inside the guarded region, e.g.:
```python
raw = bytes.fromhex(pub_hex)
if len(raw) == 65 and raw[0] == 0x04:
    raw = raw[1:]
vk = VerifyingKey.from_string(raw, curve=NIST256p)
```

The private key string (PEM or hex) is a signing secret, but its format is decided by a substring test on the raw value. Two problems:
1. `_load_signing_key(prv)` calls `prv.__contains__` directly; passing a `None` or non-str value (e.g. a missing `auth.private_key`) raises a confusing `TypeError` instead of a clear error.
2. Encoding assumptions are implicit: the hex path uses `bytes.fromhex` which requires an even-length hex string (needs an explicit `ValueError` for invalid input), and the PEM path assumes a valid PEM block. Both raise ValueError with no context about what input was rejected.
Consider validating the input type and wrapping key-parse errors in a descriptive message so callers can distinguish a bad key from a signing failure.

`generate_bd_ticket_client_data` builds the string to be signed using an f-string with unescaped `ticket` and `api` values. If a ticket or path value legitimately contains `&` or `=`, the resulting `req_content` ("ticket,path,timestamp") no longer unambiguously maps to `res_sign`, and verification on the server side can fail or, worse, an attacker-controlled ticket could inject extra query parameters into the signed payload. Percent-encode the component values (e.g. `urllib.parse.quote`) before assembling the signature string so the signed content is canonical.

items.content: The module-level `_cache` dict is shared mutable state. In multi-threaded use, concurrent calls can interleave the check-then-act update on `_cache["token"]`/`_cache["ts"]`, and the cached token is global regardless of the `ttwid`/`proxies` used, so a token fetched with one identity may be returned for a different one. The response body is never checked for HTTP status and `resp` is not closed deterministically. More importantly, `token` is extracted only from the response header/Set-Cookie; any non-2xx response (e.g. 403/429) yields an empty token that is silently returned. Consider checking `resp.status_code` before parsing and closing the response.

The profile provides `webgl_vendor` / `webgl_renderer` (see `utils/fingerprint.py`), and `get_profile()`'s docstring states it unifies "UA/几何/硬件", but `build_fingerprint()` never writes them anywhere: the template's `"webgl": {}` is emitted empty. The result is a fingerprint that advertises no WebGL vendor/renderer while the same process profile selected a GPU preset, and those two profile keys are currently consumed nowhere in the repository. Populate the `webgl` object (or drop the unused profile keys) so the report body matches the profile actually used for the HTTP layer.

Counter increment is inconsistent and the shared counter is unused. `generate_xbogus` increments a local copy via `counter += 1`, so the caller's value is never advanced. `XbogusSigner.sign` compensates by incrementing `self.counter` after each call, but callers of the module-level `generate_xbogus` (with their own counter) will never see it advance, and any direct call with a fixed counter emits the same `counter`-derived bytes every time. Either increment the counter in one place (e.g. return the new value / mutate the signer state) or document clearly that `generate_xbogus` takes the pre-increment value.

`bytes.fromhex(stub_hex)` raises `ValueError` on malformed/odd-length input and `TypeError` when `stub_hex` is `None`. The public `sign` API does not validate `stub_hex` before use, so a caller passing a non-hex string (e.g. a raw MD5 hex of the wrong length is fine, but any non-hex characters are not) gets an opaque crash deep inside the crypto path. Consider validating input or converting with a clear error message.

items.content: On non-Windows the process is only sent SIGTERM (`os.kill(pid, 15)`) and no verification/retry is performed, yet the function reports it as `killed`. If the target ignores or blocks SIGTERM (or is a zombie), `kill_all` silently leaks it and the caller logs '已终止本进程拉起的守护 pid=...' for a process that is still alive. Consider a short post-kill liveness re-check (with SIGKILL escalation on POSIX) and only appending PIDs that are actually gone.

items.content: `parse()` assumes each received chunk contains whole, complete frames. TCP reads can split a frame across `recv()` boundaries (or deliver multiple frames). For a length-126/127 frame whose payload has not fully arrived, `struct.unpack(">H"/">Q", ...)` can raise, and for a masked incomplete frame `b[i+off:i+off+ln]` silently yields a short slice — both cause the Ping/heartbeat to be miscounted, and the raised exception is swallowed by `handle()`'s `except Exception: pass`, silently dropping the connection. Since this harness's whole point is counting Ping vs hb frames precisely, buffer the bytes and only parse complete frames (retain the trailing partial frame for the next `recv`), or at minimum skip frames where `i + off + ln > len(b)`.

`got` is a module-level dict mutated by multiple per-connection threads (`handle()` does `got["conns"] += 1`, `got["ping"] += 1`, `got["hb"] += 1`), and read on the main thread for the final assertions. Read-modify-write on a dict value is not atomic, so concurrent connections can interleave increments and undercount. Guard the counters with a `threading.Lock` (or use a thread-safe counter) to make the measured results trustworthy.

`parse_ws_frames` reads `buf[i+1]` and the extended-length bytes without first confirming those bytes exist in the buffer (only `i + 2 <= len(buf)` is checked). A TCP read can deliver a partial frame, so `struct.unpack(">H", buf[i+2:i+4])[0]` / the `>Q` slice can raise `struct.error` on a short read, and the masked key slice can silently truncate. On the server this exception is swallowed by the broad `except Exception` in `handle`, silently dropping frames and skewing the counters. Guard the length before slicing, or accumulate across recv calls.

items.content: The `seen` set deduplicates by nickname, and `seen.add(nick)` happens before the comment is read. items.content: `AnimatePresence` must be a **direct child** of `LazyMotion`, but here `m.div` sits between them inside `<main>`. As written, switching `key={tab}` makes the outgoing child exit through `AnimatePresence` outside the `m.div` that would carry the feature set, so the exit animation can silently fall back to the full runtime or not run at all. `decodeURIComponent` is applied blindly to the base64 payload (after the comma of a `data:` URI). Base64 alphabet includes `+` and `/` but not `%`, so any literal `%` here does NOT belong to the base64 data — however a valid base64 payload may still legitimately contain a `%` only as part of an encoded URL fragment that got glued on (handled by the regex strip below). The risk is the opposite: a legitimately-encoded `%xx` sequence inside the *data* portion would be silently rewritten by decoders, and more importantly `decodeURIComponent` throws on any stray `%` not followed by two hex digits (caught, so it keeps raw text). Since the goal is only to strip glued-on `[原图] ...` URL remnants, prefer splitting on `[原图]`/non-base64 boundaries *before* decoding, or only decodeURIComponent when the string actually contains a `%` escape. At minimum document why `+` is not preserved as-is when it results from decoding.

<select style={{ ...inputStyle, maxWidth: 320 }} value={routePick[kind] || ""}
                onChange={(e) => routeAdd(kind, e.target.value)}>

items.content: `routeDraft`/`bindDraft`/`fbDraft` 采用「本地编辑草稿 + 统一保存」，但三个 useEffect 都只在 `q.data` 变化时初始化一次。react-query 配置了 `staleTime: 10_000`，任一 mutation 成功后都会 `refresh()` 触发后台重新拉取，若在用户编辑链路草稿期间后台返回新数据，`q.data` 引用变化会触发 `if (q.data && routeDraft === null)` 之外的 `setFbDraft(fallbackId)`（兜底 useEffect 无 `=== null` 守卫），会静默覆盖用户正在编辑的兜底选择；同理 bindDraft 若已非 null 则不会重算，草稿与实际数据可能不一致。建议统一使用 dirty 标记（如仅当用户未编辑时才同步）来避免草稿被覆盖。

The `open`/`setOpen` accordion toggle is wired to a plain `<div onClick>`, which is not keyboard accessible and lacks ARIA semantics (no role, aria-expanded, tabIndex, or keydown handler). Screen-reader and keyboard users cannot expand/collapse the card. Consider using a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` or adding `role="button"`, `tabIndex={0}`, `onKeyDown` (Enter/Space), and `aria-expanded={open}`.

Nested ternary in the success toast (project rule: “Nested ternary expressions are not allowed”). The `approve`/`revoke`/`mode` mapping is also easy to get wrong as the operator set grows. Replace with a lookup/`if`-based builder.

This fire-and-forget cleanup uses promise chaining instead of `async/await` and swallows every failure. If `gatewayOverview()` fails, the stale pending entries stay forever (the exact “明明删了还在” confusion the comment claims to fix) with no user feedback. Note the overview payload already contains `pending`, so refetching here is unnecessary if the caller passes it in.

`testing` holds a single id, so the in-flight guard is lost as soon as another channel is tested: the first button flips back to “测试推送” while its request is still running, allowing duplicate concurrent test pushes. Track the set of in-flight ids instead.
items.suggestion_code: const [testing, setTesting] = useState<Set<string>>(new Set());

items.content: Saving posts the whole merged `cfg` object. The backend stores gateway settings (mode/grants/pending) in the same file, so any gateway change that happens between draft load and save (the gateway overview is polled every 15s and grants are approved from this very panel) gets clobbered by the stale `gateway` subtree returned earlier from `/api/notify/config`. Consider sending only `{enabled, channels, llm}` / re-fetching config right before save, or have the backend merge section-wise.

Massive duplication: the exact same ~600-char Tailwind button className string is copy-pasted 8 times in this file (test/fetch/edit/delete/new/cancel/save plus the row buttons). Any design-token change (e.g. `--ease-spring`, `disabled:opacity-40`) must now be edited in 8 places and will inevitably drift. `settings-shared.tsx` already exists as the shared layer for this section group — extract e.g. `btnSecondary` / `btnPrimary` / `btnDanger` class constants there and reuse them.

`testPvMut.isPending` / `fetchMut.isPending` are global flags of a single mutation instance, so while testing provider A every other provider's 「测密钥」/「拉取模型」button in the list is also disabled. Worse, the 拉取模型 button label `拉取中…` is rendered for *all* rows, so the user cannot tell which provider is actually being fetched. Track the in-flight provider id (e.g. `testPvMut.variables` / a state field) and disable/label per row.

The header comment claims `Block`(ModelHubSection) and `Section`(AgentSection) were "逐字节相同" and merged here, and that `errMsg` was de-duplicated across 6 files — but `inputStyle` (line 56) is still declared locally in `AgentSection.tsx` (line ~406) *and* exported here, so AgentSection keeps its own duplicate. The stated goal ("各 Section 只引用不重复定义") is not actually achieved; either migrate `AgentSection.tsx` to import `inputStyle` from this module or update the comment so it does not overstate the completed dedup.

`sel` is only a tag **lookup**; if the selected tag disappears from the list (e.g. deleted in another tab, or after a refetch) `sel` becomes `null` but `selId` is still truthy, so the `{selId && ...}` block keeps rendering with `sel?.name` === undefined and "正在编辑标签「undefined」的参数" is shown to the user. Guard the render blocks with `sel` instead of `selId`.
items.existing_code: const sel = tags.find((t: ConfigTagSummary) => t.id === selId) || null;
items.suggestion_code:
const sel = tags.find((t: ConfigTagSummary) => t.id === selId) || null;
  // 注意：删除/刷新后 sel 可能为 null，渲染分支应使用 sel 而非 selId

items.content: Inconsistent fallback semantics produce a misleading label. `bound = bindings[name] || ""` already converts an empty string to `""`, so the `|| ""` has no effect and cannot distinguish "not bound" from "binding to an unknown/stale tag id". When the bound tag id is not present in `tags` (deleted on the server / stale cache), `boundName` is undefined and the UI shows "全局", which is wrong — the account is still bound to a non-existent tag. Fall back to "未知标签" (or refresh the tag list) when `bound` is non-empty but has no matching tag.
items.suggestion_code: const bound = bindings[name] ?? "";

items.content: The `<select>` is driven by the server value but every change fires a mutation without any optimistic update or per-account pending state, so the UI snaps back to the old value until the refetch completes; a rapid second change can also race (no serialization). Consider tracking a pending mutation per account (or optimistic `setQueryData` on success/failure rollback) to keep the control responsive and consistent.
items.existing_code:
<select
                  value={bound}
                  onChange={(e) =>
                    bindMut.mutate({ account: name, tagId: e.target.value })
                  }
items.suggestion_code:
<select
                  value={bound}
                  disabled={bindMut.isPending}
                  onChange={(e) =>
                    bindMut.mutate({ account: name, tagId: e.target.value })
                  }

items.content: `delMut` never sets `disabled={delMut.isPending}`, so the delete button stays clickable after the first click and the deletion request can be fired multiple times (double-click → two DELETE calls, repeated confirmations/errors).
items.suggestion_code:
if (delMut.isPending) return;
                    delMut.mutate(selId);

items.content: The delete handler dereferences `sel?.name` (already null-guarded) but then unconditionally calls `delMut.mutate(selId)`. Since `selId` can be non-empty while `sel` is `null` (see the `sel` lookup issue), this would target a tag the user never selected/confirmed. Use `sel.id` (or bail out when `!sel`) so the confirmation text and the deleted id always refer to the same tag.

`bindMut.success` does not invalidate the `["unified-settings", scope]` queries that `UnifiedConfigSection` uses to build its config (base + scoped overlay). A rebind therefore leaves scalar/agent/session config editors (including the active `tag-switcher` list) showing the previously bound tag's data until a manual refresh.

The numeric input keeps a raw string on every keystroke via `props.onChange("")` and via `commit()`'s rounding, which means the parent's stored value for an `int` field can transiently be `""` (empty string) or a rounded number while the user is still typing. Combined with `value={String(value ?? "")}`, typing e.g. "12" then "3" resets the caret and can normalize (round) mid-typing, making the field jumpy. Consider keeping a local draft string state for the input and only propagating the parsed value on blur/commit.

`Number(raw)` accepts values like `"0x10"` (16), `"1e3"` (1000) and `"  12  "` for `int` fields, and `Math.round` silently truncates decimals typed into an `int` field (e.g. `1.7` becomes `2`) instead of reporting an error. Validate with `Number.isInteger` for `int` and reject exponent/hex forms so that invalid input is surfaced via `setErr` rather than silently coerced.

The validation error state is local to `SchemaField` (`useState("")`) and is never cleared when the field's `value` is updated externally (e.g. after a successful save or a "恢复默认" reset the parent passes a new value). `err` persists, so the input keeps its red border and stale error text even though the value is now valid. Reset `err` in a `useEffect` keyed on the incoming `props.value` (or clear it in the reset/save flow).

`saveMut.isPending` is passed as the `saving` prop for every `SectionCard`, so while saving one section all sections show as "保存中…" and their save/reset buttons are disabled. Track the pending section (e.g. `saveMut.variables === sec.key`) so only the affected card is locked.

The `queryKey` includes `historyPage`, and the queryFn always calls `getTaskHistory(PAGE_SIZE, historyPage * PAGE_SIZE)` with a computed offset. This is not real pagination: every page change issues a request that returns `list` for the *current page only*, and `historyQ.data.list` is used directly as the display list. Combined with the refresh handler, this creates an inconsistency:

- `refreshHistory()` forces `setHistoryPage(0)` and then invalidates `["task-history"]`. React Query invalidation matches by prefix, but the page reset and the invalidation are batched, so the visible list may momentarily be built from page 0 data while the stored page is still >0 — and the "清空" button is rendered based on `history.length`, which comes from whatever page is currently cached.

Consider accumulating pages into a single list (e.g. `useInfiniteQuery`) so that `history.length`/`historyTotal` stay consistent with what the user has loaded, rather than treating a single server page as if it were cumulative.

The `已显示 {history.length} / {historyTotal} 条` label is also misleading when a page other than 0 is active: `history.length` will report only the current page size (≤ 50), not the cumulative count.

`refreshHistory` resets `historyPage` to 0 and immediately invalidates the `["task-history"]` prefix. Because the component reads the data of the *current* `historyPage` key, after clearing history on page N>0 the component first renders the (now stale/empty) query for page N, and the invalidation refetches `["task-history", 0]` — a key the component may no longer be reading once the state update lands, leaving the component bound to a query that was never refetched (only the exact key that is mounted gets refetched). This can leave the table showing stale rows after a clear. Either invalidate only after the state update has been committed, or drop the local paging state entirely.

`setTimeout(..., 150)` schedules a state update side effect (`props.goReview`) that is never cancelled on unmount. If the user navigates away within the 150 ms window, the callback fires after the component is unmounted, calling `goReview` on a stale closure and potentially switching tabs back unexpectedly. Store the timer id and clear it in a `useEffect` cleanup (or await `setTab` via a callback instead of a magic delay). Also, the hardcoded 150 ms delay is a fragile assumption about how long the tab switch takes to propagate.

The four engine control buttons (`pause`/`resume`/`stop`/`stop`) fire the API call and then push a success toast that is shown unconditionally, without inspecting the response. If the backend returns `{ ok: false }` (e.g. the task already finished, or a state-transition guard rejects the request), the UI still tells the user "已暂停"/"已停止", which is misleading. Check `r.ok` and surface the backend error (or refetch `overview`) before reporting success — the `exportStats` handler in this same file already does this correctly and can serve as the pattern.
items.existing_code:
api
                              .stop()
                              .then(() => push("已硬停止，存量私信终止发送"))

items.content: `clearTaskHistory()` swallows every failure via `.catch(() => {})`: the user clicks "清空" and, if the request fails (network error, permission denial, server error), nothing at all happens on screen — no error message and no state change. Silent swallowing of errors contradicts the async error-handling requirement; surface the error with `push("清空失败: " + errMsg(e))` at minimum.

The reuse mapping reads `cfg.forceRescan` (camelCase) and `cfg.maxTarget`, but the persisted config snapshot is typed as `Partial<TaskConfigSnapshot>`, whose fields are snake_case (`force_rescan`, `max_target`). The local extension only declares `live_url`, `max_target`, `live_id`, and `dm_pool`, so `cfg.forceRescan` and `cfg.maxTarget` are not part of the declared shape and will always be `undefined` for a real snapshot — the "强制重新扫描" setting is silently dropped when reusing a task. Read `cfg.force_rescan` (and drop the dead camelCase fallbacks) unless the persistence layer actually normalizes to camelCase, in which case the type declaration should be updated instead.
