room: cfg.live_url || cfg.live_id || "",
      maxTarget: cfg.max_target ?? cfg.maxTarget,
      interval: cfg.interval,
      delay: cfg.delay,
      dmPool: Array.isArray(cfg.dm_pool) ? cfg.dm_pool : cfg.dmPool,
      forceRescan: cfg.forceRescan,

items.content: `ov.liveUrl` is never produced by the `Overview` API response (see `Overview` in api/client.ts, which has no `liveUrl` field), so the "目标" column prints the `—` placeholder for every running task rather than the live room URL. Either the field is genuinely missing from the backend payload (in which case the column is dead UI) or the display should read from the current-task/config source — it should not rely on a field the API contract does not define.

`pick` returns `T` but accesses `arr[Math.floor(...)]`, which is `T | undefined` under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. More importantly, calling `pick([])` returns `undefined` at runtime while the signature promises `T`, leading to null-pointer errors downstream. Add a guard or document the precondition.

Division by zero when `pts.length === 1`: `x(i)` computes `i / (pts.length - 1)` = `0/0` = NaN, producing an invalid SVG path. Also `Math.max(...pts)` / `Math.min(...pts)` on a large array can blow the call stack. Guard the single-point case (or accept a defensive early return).
items.suggestion_code:
const n = pts.length;
  const x = (i: number) => (n > 1 ? (i / (n - 1)) * w : 0);

items.content: `hue(i)` with a negative index returns `HUES[negative]` = `undefined`, producing the invalid CSS `oklch(55% 0.14 undefined)` in `Avatar`. Normalize the index to be non-negative.

The `Dot` prop `c` is typed as a loose `string` and the color resolution uses `c.includes(...)` substring matching, which is fragile: `"warn-danger"` or any mixed string silently matches the first branch, and there is no type safety. Prefer a union type `"ok" | "warn" | "danger" | "accent" | "mute" | "pulse"` with an explicit map.
items.existing_code: export function Dot({ c, pulse }: { c: string; pulse?: boolean }) {

items.content: The `Avatar` `h` prop is a raw string interpolated directly into the CSS value `oklch(55% 0.14 ${h})`. If any caller passes user-controlled input this becomes CSS injection; at minimum validate/normalize to a numeric hue and provide a numeric type (`h: number`).

Inconsistent spacing model across the Card family: `CardContent` hardcodes `p-4`, while `CardFooter` overrides only the top padding (`p-4 pt-0`) and `CardHeader` uses `p-4`. When `CardFooter` is composed under `CardContent` the content is double-padded (16px + 16px) between them. Consider moving padding to the Card/Header/Content level consistently (e.g. let children own padding, or expose a shared spacing token) so composed cards don't need per-usage padding overrides — note most call sites already pass `p-2.5`/`p-3.5` to override `p-4`, which suggests the default is not the intended design value.

`CardTitle` and `CardDescription` are plain function components with no `forwardRef`, unlike every other primitive in this directory (button.tsx, input.tsx, dialog.tsx, tabs.tsx, etc. all use `React.forwardRef`). This blocks ref access (focus management, aria-labelledby wiring, measuring) for consumers and is inconsistent with the library's convention. Wrap them in `React.forwardRef<HTMLHeadingElement, ...>` / `React.forwardRef<HTMLParagraphElement, ...>`.

Accessibility defect: the close button's only accessible label is a hardcoded Chinese string "关闭", and the `DialogPrimitive.Close` element has no `aria-label`/`title`. Since DialogContent is also missing the required `aria-describedby` fallback and the trigger is not wired to an accessible name, screen readers may announce the close control ambiguously (the `sr-only` span text is fine but depends on it being rendered before the icon — currently the icon comes first, so the label ordering is icon-then-text; ensure the label precedes/annotates the button). Consider adding `aria-label="Close"` on the button and keeping the visible-language text configurable.

`value` is destructured out of props and used only for the inline transform, but it is never forwarded to `ProgressPrimitive.Root`. Radix's Root relies on `value`/`max` to derive `aria-valuenow`, `data-state` and `data-value`; without it radix falls back to `max`, so the bar visually moves but is announced to assistive tech as fully complete/indeterminate — an accessibility defect. Pass `value` (and let `max` flow through) to the Root, e.g. `value={value}`.

Hardcoded color literal `rgba(128,128,128,0.2)` bypasses the project's design-token convention. The sibling components use CSS variables (e.g. `bg-[var(--color-border)]` in separator.tsx), so the scrollbar thumb will not follow theme changes / dark mode. Prefer a theme token such as `bg-[var(--color-border)]` or the project's muted-foreground token.
items.suggestion_code: <ScrollAreaPrimitive.Thumb className="relative flex-1 rounded-full bg-[var(--color-border)]" />

items.content: For `position="popper"`, Radix requires the popper content to supply its own `--radix-select-content-available-height` based sizing/animation states; the hardcoded `max-h-96` here conflicts with the popper's available-height calculation and can make the dropdown overflow the viewport (no `overflow-y-auto` is applied either). Also `translate-y-1` is applied unconditionally for popper, which disables Radix's data-state based animations. Consider using `data-[side=bottom]:translate-y-1`, `data-[side=top]:-translate-y-1` and a viewport-level `max-h`/`overflow-y-auto` consistent with the shadcn reference implementation.

`fmtAgo` clamps the delta to 0 via `Math.max(0, ...)`, so any timestamp in the future (clock skew between browser and server, or a bad `create_time`) is rendered as `0秒前`. A future timestamp should be handled explicitly (e.g. return `刚刚`/empty or the absolute time) rather than silently reported as "0 seconds ago", which hides data errors.

`fmtNum` does not guard against non-finite values: `Infinity` passes every `>=` branch and produces `Infinity亿`, and `Number.NaN` is only caught because `Number.isNaN` is checked. Consider using `Number.isFinite(n)` instead of the null/undefined/NaN combination so `Infinity`/`-Infinity` also fall back to the placeholder.
items.existing_code: if (n === null || n === undefined || Number.isNaN(n)) return "—";
items.suggestion_code: if (n === null || n === undefined || !Number.isFinite(n)) return "—";

items.content: `fmtTime` blindly multiplies its input by 1000 (treating it as a Unix-seconds value), but callers are inconsistent: `live-page.tsx` passes `f.ts`/`r.captured_at` (seconds) while other places convert to milliseconds before formatting. Since there is no unit documented in the signature and no guard for millisecond input, a caller passing ms will silently render a wildly wrong date. Document the expected unit (Unix seconds) in the JSDoc and/or validate the range.

The non-null assertion `!` assumes the `#root` element always exists. If index.html changes or the script is loaded before the DOM node exists, `getElementById` returns `null` and `createRoot(null)` throws an opaque runtime error. Add an explicit null check for a clear failure message.

Type inconsistency: `key`/`AppShell.setTab` uses `TabId`, but `if (PAGES[t]) setKey(t)` relies on an unchecked index. Since `t` is `TabId` the guard is fine, but `SegmentedTabs.onChange` calls `PAGES[k].tab` directly without a guard — if `k` is ever not a page key this will throw `Cannot read property 'tab' of undefined`. Prefer a safe lookup like `PAGES[k]?.tab ?? spec.tab`, or keep a `hasPage` check consistent with the other handler.
items.suggestion_code: onChange={(k) => { const s = PAGES[k]; if (!s) return; setKey(k); setTab(s.tab); }}

items.content: `BASE_PROPS` is cast with `as PageProps` after `as never`-style mock, silently defeating type checking. Several page props (goMsg, goDm, setTab, goReview, reviewPayload, goReuse, reusePayload, msgAcct, setMsgAcct, refreshState, setRefreshState, ...) are missing. Downstream pages may dereference these undefined callbacks at runtime (e.g. `props.goReview(...)`), producing crashes that are hard to distinguish from real regressions during visual verification. Consider providing safe default stubs for the callback props so the harness fails less misleadingly.

The whole mock API object is cast to `never` (`} as never;`), which disables all type checking against the real `typeof api`. Any signature drift between the mock and the real client (e.g. changed return shape or renamed method) will not be caught here; also `MOCK_OVERVIEW as never` is an unsafe cast. Prefer typing the mock as `Partial<typeof api>` or `typeof api` so mismatches surface at compile time.

`VIEW_TITLE` is declared as `Record<ViewType, string>` but is missing entries for the source views the union is documented to be a superset of. Because the union itself is also incomplete the object currently type-checks, masking the inconsistency (see the `SOURCE_VIEWS` comment). Making the union/`VIEW_TITLE` consistent, or typing this as `Record<(typeof SOURCE_VIEWS)[number] | ViewType, string>`, would surface the gap at compile time.

`overflow: hidden` on `body` (and `#root { height: 100vh }`) makes the page completely unscrollable. In a WebView2/WKWebView shell this also hides the vertical scrollbar and can clip content in short windows; if any view relies on document-level scrolling, content becomes unreachable for keyboard-only users. It is also unnecessary since `#root` already constrains height. Suggest `overflow: clip` on `html, body` only if truly needed, or drop it and let inner scroll containers handle overflow.

`--radius-sm: 8px` is set here, but the global focus ring uses `border-radius: var(--radius-sm)` on `:focus-visible`. This forces an 8px radius override onto every focused element (inputs, buttons, custom chips), visually mutating non-square focus targets and conflicting with their own `rounded-*` classes. The focus ring should not alter the element's computed border-radius — prefer `outline` alone, or use `outline-offset` without re-declaring radius.

Specificity conflict with the design intent: `.glass-premium` declares `backdrop-filter: blur(48px)`, yet the earlier `html:not([data-glass-frost]) .glass-premium` rule has higher specificity (element + attribute + class) and always wins in the default state, so the documented 48px premium blur can never take effect. The frost override should use the same or lower specificity, or the base declarations should live in a rule that the override can legitimately beat.

The `shimmer` keyframes are declared at top level (outside `@theme`), but Tailwind v4 only emits keyframes that are referenced by an `--animate-*` theme token; the hand-written `animation: shimmer 2.5s infinite` in `.animate-shimmer` may therefore reference a keyframe that is stripped/not tokenized. Consider declaring `--animate-shimmer: shimmer 2.5s infinite;` (and similarly for `pulse-dot`, `orb-drift`, `spin-custom`, `nebula-pulse`) inside `@theme` so Tailwind keeps the keyframes.

Dead code: `defaultAccent()` (and `DEFAULT_ACCENT`) are exported but never referenced anywhere in the frontend (only `ThemeId`, `normalizeGlowId`, `resolveAccent` are imported by ThemeContext). `rgbToHsv` / `hsvToRgb` are also exported yet have zero call sites in the whole repo. Either remove them or add the intended consumer (e.g. the color picker) — otherwise this is dead surface that must be maintained.

Dead code: `rgbToHsv` / `hsvToRgb` have no callers anywhere in the frontend (verified by repo-wide search). Unused exported helpers with non-trivial math are a maintenance liability — delete them or wire them into the color-picker UI.

Bug (silent color inversion): in the dark (`aerospace`) branch, a custom hex is repeatedly blended toward white by 8% up to 24 times. For a dark custom accent the loop overshoots badly — e.g. `#101010` ends up around `#dedede`, i.e. the user picks black and the UI renders near-white (and `onColorFor` then flips the ink to dark). The loop should clamp the amount of lightening (e.g. cap iterations / stop once within the target band, or lerp directly to the band instead of iterating), so a user's dark color is nudged rather than inverted.

`resolveAccent` returns `ACCENTS[0]` for any unrecognized value, so this reader cannot distinguish "unset" from "unrecognized", and the `"green"` literal duplicates `DEFAULT_ACCENT` (accents.ts exports it). Validate the raw stored value first and fall back to the exported default to stay in sync if the default preset ever changes.

Inconsistent validation with `setGlow`. `setGlow` explicitly normalizes via `normalizeGlowId`, but `setAccent` relies on `resolveAccent`'s silent fallback, meaning an invalid accent passed here is silently replaced by `ACCENTS[0]` and then *persisted*. Use the exported `isValidAccent`/`DEFAULT_ACCENT` to normalize explicitly so the API behaves predictably and the intent is documented.

The dynamic import of `@tauri-apps/plugin-shell` is untyped (`any`), which hides the fact that the fallback branch is effectively dead code in a Tauri build and makes the return type unsafe. Prefer typing the module (`typeof import('@tauri-apps/plugin-shell')`) instead of `any`, so `mod?.open` type-checks and the reason for any fallback is explicit.
items.existing_code:
const mod: any = await import("@tauri-apps/plugin-shell");
    const open = mod?.open;

items.content: `window.open` returns `Window | null` and does not throw; it returns `null` when the popup is blocked. The current code always returns `true` here, so callers cannot detect a failed open (popup blocker, non-Tauri web build). Return `window.open(...) !== null` so a blocked popup is reported as failure.

Same issue in the catch fallback: `window.open` does not throw on failure (it returns `null`), so the inner `try/catch` never triggers and the function always reports success. Use the returned value to determine the result.
items.suggestion_code: return window.open(url, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer") !== null;

items.content: The doc comment states `shell:allow-open` permission is required (see src-tauri/capabilities/default.json), but the catch block only logs to console and silently falls back. When `open` exists but throws (typically a missing/denied permission in Tauri), the fallback `window.open` inside a WebView silently fails — exactly the bug this utility was written to fix. Consider surfacing this failure to the caller (and/or user) rather than swallowing it, e.g. check `window.__TAURI__` / `isTauri()` to distinguish "not running in Tauri" from "permission denied".

items.content: alias 值 `/src` 是根路径写法：它依赖 Vite “以 / 开头即相对 project root” 的隐式约定，而不是显式文件路径。本项目前端由根目录 `npm run dev --workspace frontend` 启动（见 tauri.conf.json 的 beforeDevCommand），root 恰好仍是 frontend，所以目前能工作；但一旦 Vite 以仓库根为 root 运行（例如新增根级 vite 配置、或在 monorepo 根执行构建），该别名会静默指向不存在的 `<root>/src`，表现为「模块找不到」的诡异报错。建议改为显式路径：`import { fileURLToPath, URL } from "node:url"` 后使用 `"@": fileURLToPath(new URL("./src", import.meta.url))`。

`Set-Location $scriptDir` changes the process-wide working directory and it is never restored (the `finally` block only removes the temp file). `git add`/`git commit` operate on the CWD, so the script silently relocates the caller's location for the rest of the session and commits the script's repo — if the user invoked it from another repo/directory, or runs several commands afterwards, the results are wrong. Restore the previous location in `finally` (and/or pass `-C $scriptDir` to git instead of relying on the global CWD).
items.suggestion_code:
$scriptDir = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
$prevLocation = Get-Location
Set-Location $scriptDir

items.content: `ReadAllText` decodes the file with UTF-8 by default, but if `_commit_msg.txt` was actually written in GBK/ANSI (the very encoding problem this script exists to avoid) the non-ASCII bytes become U+FFFD replacement characters, so the commit message is silently corrupted before being re-encoded to UTF-8. Detect the encoding first (e.g. via `[System.Text.Encoding]::Default`/BOM sniffing) or fail loudly instead of silently mojibaking the message.

Empty message is not validated. With `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` an empty/whitespace-only `_commit_msg.txt` gets passed to `git commit -F`, which aborts the commit (and leaves the index staged, since `git add` already ran) — a confusing failure. Validate that the trimmed content is non-empty before running `git add`/`git commit` and give a clear error.

`git add @Paths` splats the array directly; file paths are then interpreted by git as pathspecs/options. Two problems: (1) a path beginning with `-` (or containing pathspec magic like a leading `:`) is treated as an option/revision rather than a file; (2) default PowerShell wildcard globbing on path arguments means a name containing `[`/`*` may expand unexpectedly. Consider disabling globbing (`-Path`-safe handling; git's pathspecs are already globs) and passing `'--'` before the file list to terminate option parsing, e.g. `git add -- @Paths`.
items.suggestion_code: git add -- @Paths

items.content: If anything in the `try` block throws (e.g. `git commit` fails, or an invalid path is passed), the script exits with the exception propagated but never surfaces a clear message — and because `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` makes native-command failures non-fatal in PS 5.1 only via exit codes (not exceptions), `git commit` returning non-zero may still print "[ok] commit done". Check `$LASTEXITCODE` after `git commit` and report failure/exit non-zero instead of unconditionally claiming success.

Non-standard field `allowScripts` is not a recognized package.json key (npm uses `scripts`/`config`; pnpm/yarn use different mechanisms). If the intent is to allow a postinstall build script, this key is silently ignored, meaning `esbuild@0.21.5`'s install script may still be blocked by package managers that gate lifecycle scripts, breaking the build unexpectedly. Consider using the tool-specific supported config (e.g., npm `overrides`/`.npmrc`, or remove this dead config).

The build script defaults to `onefile` mode because it invokes `build_sidecar.py` without `--onedir`, while build_sidecar.py's own docs state onefile is the legacy/slow mode (~114MB unpacked to %TEMP% on every start) and onedir is the intended fast path. The cleanup block below only deletes the flat `*.exe` files, which is also the onefile output layout, so the two halves are coupled to the slow mode. Recommend passing `--onedir` explicitly (and forwarding user args) so the shipped sidecar uses the onedir/shared-_internal layout.
items.suggestion_code: & $PY $script --onedir

items.content: `build_sidecar.py` is not validated before being invoked. If the script is missing (e.g. wrong $root, or a partial checkout), PowerShell will report a command-not-found error, but because $LASTEXITCODE may retain a stale value from a previous native command the subsequent `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0)` check is not a reliable failure signal here. Add an explicit existence check and exit 1, consistent with the $PY check above.

Cleanup is incomplete: it only removes the flat `<name>-<triple>.exe` files, but `build_sidecar.py` in onedir mode produces `src-tauri\binaries\<name>-<triple>\` directories plus a shared `_internal\` directory. A stale onedir output will not be cleaned, and the comment's stated rationale (avoiding safe-delete interception when PyInstaller overwrites an existing exe) does not hold for that layout. Also, `Remove-Item ... -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` silently ignores failures, so a leftover locked exe passes unnoticed. Consider removing the mode-specific artifacts and verifying deletion succeeded before proceeding.

The hard-coded absolute fallback path (including a specific Windows user name `LOX` and a personal desktop directory) and the hard-coded interpreter path `C:\Users\LOX\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python314\python.exe` are machine-specific. This contradicts the stated intent that the tool is a general product, makes the script unusable on other machines (including CI), and leaks a local user path. Prefer deriving the root from `$PSScriptRoot` unconditionally (failing clearly if it cannot be resolved) and resolving Python via an env var (e.g. `$env:DY_PYTHON`) or `py -3`, falling back to `Get-Command python` with a warning rather than a hard-coded path.

The `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` triple is hard-coded here while `build_sidecar.py::_target_triple()` derives it from `platform.machine()`. On an arm64 machine the cleanup step would look for `dyautodm-backend-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe` while the build produces `...-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.exe`, so stale artifacts would never be removed. Since `$PY` is invoked anyway, derive the triple the same way (e.g. `& $PY -c "import sys;print(...)"`) or at least compute the arch from `$env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` to keep the two in sync.

`_write_version_file()` swallows any exception and returns the version anyway, after which `main()` proceeds to build. If the write fails (permissions, read-only checkout, disk full), the sidecar is packaged with a stale or missing `backend/_build_version.py`, silently defeating the front/back version-mismatch check that this script exists to guarantee. A failed version injection should abort the build (raise / sys.exit) rather than continuing.

When a target file exists but its version cannot be extracted (missing/malformed `version` key, no `BUILD_VERSION` match, unparsable JSON), `_extract` silently returns `""`. All five files can therefore be present yet yield no version, and the failure is only reported for that individual file while the aggregate equality check treats the empty value as 'absent' rather than 'mismatched'. More importantly, `_extract` calls `path.read_text` / `json.loads` without any exception handling: a `JSONDecodeError` or `UnicodeDecodeError` aborts the whole gate with an unhandled traceback instead of the intended `exit 1` diagnostic. Wrap extraction in `try/except` and report the parse failure into `bad`.

`ls -t ... | head -1` is a fragile way to select a file: its output is line-based, so a filename containing a newline would break `$f`, and `ls` formatting/decorations in some environments can also interfere. Prefer a null-delimited, shell-native approach such as `find`/`printf '%s\n' ... | sort -r`.

items.content: `stop_browser_daemon` matches the label built with `browser_daemon({account}:{port})`, but `start_browser_daemon` never validates `account`/`port`. A caller passing an account containing `:` or `/` (or a port reproduced differently) yields a label mismatch, so the daemon silently becomes un-stoppable → orphan process holding the port. Either normalize/validate `account`/`port` on start, or key the lookup on structured fields (e.g. a typed `DaemonKey` newtype) instead of a formatted string, which also removes the fragile string-based `format!` in three places.

If a daemon handle with a matching label exists but its process has already exited, `h.kill()` is a no-op and the command returns `Ok(())`. Callers may then assume the daemon is stopped although the handle wasn't actually killed. Consider distinguishing a stale/dead handle (`h.is_alive()`) and reporting it, and use `kill_tree()` here for symmetry with the shutdown path in `on_window_event` so PyInstaller `_MEI` grandchildren are not orphaned.

`stop_recv_daemon`/`stop_browser_daemon` validate the process by matching a label string only, while the actual kill is by OS pid; conversely the port is taken from the caller verbatim. There is no validation that the pid still belongs to the process originally registered (pid reuse after the daemon exits could cause `kill_tree()` to terminate an unrelated process tree). Prefer verifying the child is still the live one registered (e.g. check `is_alive()`/the stored `CommandChild` before issuing `taskkill /F /T`), and reject/verify `port` ranges before using them in labels or process arguments.

The log-write command takes arbitrary frontend-controlled `text` and writes it unbounded into `logs/frontend_boot.log` with no size cap or rotation. A misbehaving or compromised webview can spam this call and grow the log without limit (and the file is never truncated). Bound the write (size/rate limit) and/or rely on the already-configured logger instead of a bespoke file path derived from the executable directory.

Race: the supervisor installs the new child and then sets `alive = true`. A concurrent `kill_tree()` can take the `child` lock between these two steps — it will kill the *new* child, and the supervisor's subsequent `alive.store(true)` leaves the handle reporting alive with no running process. Consider installing the child and updating `alive` under the same lock (or re-check `stopping` while holding the `child` mutex) so a concurrent stop cannot be lost.

`resolve_sidecar` already called `app.shell().sidecar(name)` and returned Err if it failed, so this `is_ok()` check can only ever be true here — the error message below ("...且 externalBin 不可用") is effectively unreachable. Moreover, per the deployment notes, `sidecar().is_ok()` can misreport Ok when the externalBin file was not actually embedded, so returning `PathBuf::from(name)` may yield a path that fails only at spawn time. Consider making this fallback explicit/best-effort (e.g. document it, or verify the resolved binary exists).

The packaged sidecar is launched without a `-WorkingDirectory`. The exe path resolves relative to the caller's current directory, so any data/config/log paths the backend derives from its working directory will be resolved against an unrelated folder, and behavior will differ between invoking the script from the repo root versus elsewhere. Pass `-WorkingDirectory $ROOT` (mirroring the `-DevBackend` branch) for consistency.

Also note the two ready checks use inconsistent timeouts (15 vs 20) with no explanation. Consider checking the response status/content explicitly and aligning the timeout constants.

The source-mode backend relies on the `py` launcher being on PATH; when `-DevBackend` is used on a machine without the launcher (or with only a Store placeholder) the process exits immediately and the user only sees the generic "[FAIL] 后端启动超时". items.content: `POST /api/messages/send` can block synchronously: the WS path waits up to 90s for the dispatch task to complete (`deadline = _t.time() + 90`), then on failure the fallback channel waits another up to 90s. Passing an invalid `conv_id="x"` guarantees the failure path, so this "contract" test may hang the suite for up to ~180s (or hit network timeouts). Pin the assertion to a fast path (e.g. keep the process in a state where the channel is unavailable immediately) or bound it with an explicit timeout.

The output path is hard-coded with an absolute, machine-specific path (C:\Users\LOX\Desktop\DYchajian\LLM-Wiki\...). This will fail on any other machine, user account, or environment, and the directory may not even exist. Consider deriving the destination from `$PSScriptRoot`/`$PWD` or accepting it as a parameter, and creating the parent directory if missing.

Consider verifying a published SHA256 hash and using fail-fast error handling, e.g. `Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $out -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop` followed by a checksum comparison.

On a hot download path this is repeated I/O; consider buffering or batching writes, and note that `_load` reads the entire file into memory on every `DownloadedCache` construction. Also, the write in `add` intentionally happens outside the lock to avoid holding it during I/O — which means concurrent `add` calls can interleave writes; on most filesystems a single `write` of `key + "\n"` is atomic enough, but it’s worth a comment documenting that assumption.

`has`/`add`/`count` are guarded by `threading.Lock`, and `TaskManager` uses `RLock`, so the module claims thread-safety — but `mark()` mutates arbitrary attributes of a `DownloadTask` that is also mutated directly by callers (e.g. `task.total_files = len(files)`, `task.save_path = out_dir` in the downloader). Those direct writes bypass the lock and race with concurrent `mark()`/`to_dict()` reads from other threads, so readers can observe a partially updated task. Either route all mutations through `mark()` or document clearly that the manager is only safe for the flag/status bookkeeping, not for direct field writes.

Dead code / scope contradiction: This barrel file's own header states the comment subsystem is "未对齐（本项目无对应业务）" — i.e. this project has no corresponding business for it. Yet `CommentRepliesState` and `CommentReplyTarget` are re-exported here. A repo-wide search shows they are referenced nowhere except their own definitions in `player-types.ts` and this re-export — no consumer imports them. This is dead code that contradicts the documented module boundary. Either remove these two exports (and the types behind them) or, if they are genuinely intended as a future public contract, document that intent explicitly instead of listing the comment subsystem as out of scope.

`ts` is declared as required (`ts: number`) in `CachedMeta`, yet `getMeta`/`setMeta` treat it as optional via `m[a].ts || 0` in the pruning sort. This inconsistency is a latent bug if legacy/partially-written entries lack `ts`. Either make `ts` optional or drop the defensive `|| 0`.

`prefetched` is a module-level mutable Set used as a one-time guard. If the player is used in an environment where the same module instance persists across long sessions with many origins (e.g., many distinct CDN hosts), this set grows unboundedly and each entry corresponds to an appended `<link rel=preconnect>` that is never removed. Consider bounding the set and/or removing stale link elements.

`link.crossOrigin = "anonymous"` is forced for every prefetch. For media origins that do not send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, a cross-origin (anonymous) preconnect may not reuse the connection that the non-CORS `<video>` request will use, defeating the purpose of the preconnect. Confirm whether `anonymous` is actually the credential mode used by the video element before hardcoding it.

`getPosition` returns `m[awemeId]?.t || 0`, so a legitimately stored `t === 0` (or a stored position that floors to 0) is indistinguishable from "no record". Since `setPosition` already rejects `seconds <= 0`, this is mostly benign, but using `?? 0` would express intent more correctly and avoid masking falsy values.

`attach` is declared `async` (returns `Promise<void>`) and callers `await k.attach(v, media)` before assuming the source is loaded, but the body is fully synchronous: it sets `el.src` and resolves immediately. Any HLS/DASH kernel added later will perform real async work (fetching manifests, attaching MediaSource), and callers currently rely on the mixed `readyState` timeout + retry logic. Consider either documenting that `attach` must resolve only after `loadedmetadata`/`canplay`, or renaming to a sync `attach`.

`onProgress` is invoked directly from `onTimeUpdate` on every time-update event (usually ~4x/second). The prop is documented as "节流后调用", and the parent enforces a 5s throttle, but relying on every caller to throttle is fragile and makes this stage dirty at high frequency. Throttle at the source (e.g. only report when `currentTime` moved >= 1s since the last report) so the contract stated in the Props docs holds.

`seek` uses `dur` captured from the render closure. During an active drag, rAF updating `dur` each frame is fine, but `v.duration` is the more authoritative source; if `dur` is still 0 (metadata not yet loaded) seek silently no-ops. More importantly, prefer reading the live duration from the media element here (`Number.isFinite(v.duration) ? v.duration : dur`) so seeking works even before the first state sync completes.

`PlayerAuthor` declares four optional fields (`nickname`, `avatar`, `signature`, `sec_uid`) but no field is required and none has a null-safety strategy; consumers destructuring `const { nickname } = author` will get `string | undefined` without any compile-time enforcement. Since this interface models data returned by the backend, consider whether at least an identifier (e.g. `sec_uid`) should be required, or whether the type should be narrowed (`Partial<PlayerAuthor>`) at the call site to make the possibility of missing fields explicit.

`PlayerStatus` includes `"rebuffering"`, and the file header documents `PLAYER_VIDEO_REBUFFER_STATUS_DELAY_MS`, but the union has no corresponding terminal/derived state description and the file provides no transition contract. More concretely: `"ready"` and `"paused"` overlap semantically with `"idle"`/`"loading"`, so consumers writing exhaustive `switch (status)` logic have no authoritative mapping. Recommend documenting the allowed transitions in the JSDoc above the union (or splitting into `PlayerStatus` + a separate buffering flag) to prevent divergent state machines across the player components.

`CommentRepliesState` / `CommentReplyTarget` are declared but, per this file's own header comment, "本项目评论能力尚未接入播放器" (comment functionality is not yet wired into the player). These are currently unreferenced exported types — dead code with no consumer. If they only exist to mirror the source project, either add a TODO/issue link stating when they will be consumed, or remove them until the comment subsystem actually lands in the player, so the file doesn't accumulate unused contracts.

Loose falsy check: `ms || 0` also converts a legitimate `0` to `0` (fine) but would coerce `NaN` to `0` silently and, more importantly, hides unexpected non-numeric inputs. Since `ms` is optional, prefer the nullish/validated form for clarity: `fmtDuration(Number.isFinite(ms) ? (ms as number) / 1000 : 0)`. This keeps the guard explicit and consistent with the `Number.isFinite` check already used in `fmtDuration`.

items.content: `s.type === "select"` fields without `options` (or with an empty options array) fall through to the plain `<input type="text">` branch, so a select field whose schema has no options silently renders as a free-text input. More importantly, for `type: "select"` the `commit()` path treats the raw string as-is — but the shared `setErr("进入数字")`-style validation is skipped correctly. Consider explicitly handling `select` and warning when options are missing, rather than silently degrading to a text input.

`commit` depends on the whole `s` schema object, so it is re-created whenever the parent re-renders with a new schema reference; the `useCallback` therefore provides no memoization benefit. Depend on the specific fields actually used (e.g. `s.type`, `s.min`, `s.max`) or use a ref/schema-keyed dependency, and also include `setErr`/destructure `props` consistently.

For a `bool` field the saved value is `Boolean(value)`, so a schema-defined string like `"false"` would be coerced to `true`. Since the parent stores `Val` (string | number | boolean) coming from a JSON schema whose `default` is `unknown`, prefer comparing against the actual boolean, e.g. `checked={value === true || value === "true" || value === 1}`, to avoid surprising coercion of string-backed flags.

`APPLY_LABEL` is referenced inside `SchemaField` (line 207) but declared at the bottom of the module. Consider moving it above `SchemaField` (or to a constants module) so the dependency direction is clear and the mapping is discoverable where it is used.

In tag mode, the success message uses the raw `scope` (tag id) to look up the label, but `scope` here shadows the outer `scope` value at closure creation time. More importantly `scope` is a tag id, yet `who` is built from the id unless `scopeName` resolves — verify the message shows the human-readable tag name rather than an opaque id. Consider reusing the same `scopeName` resolution used in the render body for consistency.

The status → tone/label mapping is duplicated with inconsistent semantics. In the running-task table the tone is `ok` for the engine, while in the history table `h.status === "running"` maps to tone `ok` (green) even though a "running" history row is only reachable when the engine is mid-run for a *different* task. More importantly, the allow-list is open-ended: any status other than `"running" | "finished"` (including `"stopped"` and any future value) falls through to `"已停止"`, so an unknown status is silently mislabeled as stopped. Centralize this mapping in one helper (e.g. in `tasks-shared.tsx`) and handle the `"stopped"` case explicitly to avoid silent mislabeling.

Also, this is a conditional (ternary) expression nested two levels deep inside the `<Tone>` prop, which the project style rules disallow; extracting a `statusMeta(status)` helper resolves both issues.

`PAGE_SIZE` is declared inside the component body, so a new value is created on every render. It is then used inside `historyQ`'s `queryFn` and in the JSX. While the value is constant, referencing a per-render variable from the query function is fragile (and if it ever became state/props it would silently change the query's meaning under an unchanged `queryKey`). Hoist it to module scope as a constant so the query key/offset derivation is stable.

The `engineTone` / `engineLabel` derivations are effectively two independent nested ternaries over the same three-state value (`stopping` / `starting` / `paused`), duplicating the state-classification logic and being easy to desynchronize (e.g. `"starting"` is `warn` in `engineTone` but has its own label branch). Prefer a single lookup table/helper that returns `{ tone, label }` for a given `engineState`/`paused` pair; nesting ternaries this deep is also disallowed by the project's style rules.

If `thumb.startswith("data:")` is true but the URI contains no comma, `thumb.find(",")` returns -1 and `thumb[0:]` yields the whole `data:...` string, which is then fed to `base64.b64decode` as a bogus payload. The resulting decode failure is swallowed by the bare `except: pass`, so such rows are silently counted as "not decodable" with no diagnostic. Guard the comma lookup (e.g. `pos = thumb.find(","); if pos < 0: continue`) and/or log the failing id so the report can distinguish real failures from parsing bugs.

The SQLite connection is opened without a `with` statement and only closed on the happy path; if `execute`/`fetchall` raises, `con.close()` is never reached and the handle leaks. Prefer `with sqlite3.connect(str(DB)) as con:` (or `contextlib.closing`) so the connection is always released.

items.content: The `[lib]` section declares `crate-type = ["staticlib", "cdylib", "rlib"]` for mobile reuse, but `tauri.conf.json` only bundles `nsis`/`msi` for Windows desktop (`bundle.targets`), and the whole sidecar-resolution logic in `src/sidecar.rs` hardcodes Windows conventions (`taskkill`, `<name>-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe`). Dropping `staticlib`/`cdylib` (keeping just `rlib`, or the default lib type) would reduce build artifacts unless iOS/Android targets are genuinely planned — otherwise the mobile-capable crate-type is misleading relative to the actual platform support.

`write_boot_log` performs blocking filesystem work (`create_dir_all`, `open`, `write`) directly inside a Tauri command; Tauri commands must be `async` or they run on the main thread, so a slow/contended disk can stall the UI. Either mark this command `async` and offload the I/O with `tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking`, or keep it infrequent and document that it is a debug-only path.

The background backend start ignores its own failure beyond logging, and the spawned task's `JoinHandle` is dropped while it holds `start_backend`'s future. If the sidecar binary is missing the app silently ends up in a state where `backend_status` returns `false` with no user-visible signal and no retry. Surface the failure (emit an event / store an error string in `AppState` that the frontend can query) instead of only `log::error!`.

The `use_external` flag is derived by comparing the resolved path against the bare sidecar name, overloading a `PathBuf` as a sentinel. If a real file matching the name happens to exist relative to the CWD, the absolute-path branch is skipped and the bare name is passed to `command()`. Returning an explicit enum from `resolve_sidecar` (e.g. `enum SidecarSource { ExternalBin, Path(PathBuf) }`) would make the two cases unambiguous and remove the stringly-typed coupling with the three call sites.

This resolve → sentinel-compare → `sidecar()`/`command()` block is duplicated verbatim in `start_python_backend`, `start_recv_daemon`, and `spawn_bcc_child`. Three copies increase the risk of drift (e.g. changing the `use_external` sentinel in only one place). Extract a helper such as `fn sidecar_builder(app, name) -> Result<Command>` and reuse it in all three starters.

Since these are full-resolution decrypted originals (~1.5 MB combined here, unbounded in general), the page blocks on every image at once and reflows when each finishes. Prefer `loading="lazy"` (or `decoding="async"`) and add `width`/`height` attributes to avoid layout shift.
